nodes.label: plates
nodes.comment: One set of continents under both countries — the point of this world is that the land is the same on either side of the emberline; only what happened to it differs.

nodes.label: warp x
nodes.comment: East-west displacement for the warp that bends plate edges into coastlines.

nodes.label: warp y
nodes.comment: The north-south half of the displacement, at a slightly different scale so the axes stay independent.

nodes.label: warped plates
nodes.comment: Straight plate bisectors become headlands, bays and island arcs.

nodes.label: rolling detail
nodes.comment: Hills and coastal wobble so the marches are not billiard-flat.

nodes.label: rolling relief
nodes.comment: A light pass of hills over the warped plates — texture, not competition.

nodes.label: basins & platform
nodes.comment: Deep basins and a low land platform. This uneroded field is the reference the lava rivers later measure carving against, so it must stay untouched by erosion.

nodes.label: drainage
nodes.comment: One drainage network for the whole world. West of the emberline it will be dressed as water, east as lava — the river remembers its course even after it catches fire.

nodes.label: eroded terrain
nodes.comment: The terrain everything stands on: valleys cut in proportion to the water they carry. The taper also digs the banks the lava rivers will glow through.

nodes.label: steepness
nodes.comment: Grade of the hillsides, so both countries trade soil for bare rock on their cliffs.

nodes.label: coast distance
nodes.comment: Shoreline distance for even-width beaches, and later the band the fens are cut from.

nodes.label: script: emberline
nodes.comment: The gradient this world hinges on: char as a function of world X alone. Fully green west of x = −768, fully burnt east of x = +768, so walking east is walking into the fire that took half the marches.

nodes.label: ember wobble
nodes.comment: Fire is not a ruler: this bends the frontier so the burnt edge meanders and bulges.

nodes.label: wobbled emberline
nodes.comment: A fifth of wobble is enough — the gradient must stay in charge or the two countries dissolve into each other.

nodes.label: ash switch
nodes.comment: The curve as a switch: near 1 where char passes 0.62, near 0 in the green — the single line the ashfall biome, the lava and the hounds all obey.

nodes.label: land switch
nodes.comment: Near 1 on dry ground, near 0 at sea — the sea never burns, and nothing spawns in the water.

nodes.label: one
nodes.comment: A constant 1, so the subtractions below can flip switches the other way around.

nodes.label: green switch
nodes.comment: 1 minus the ash switch: high wherever the fire never reached.

nodes.label: script: ward lots
nodes.comment: Which 192-tile lots hold a ward. The span matches the labyrinth below exactly — 6 chunks of 32 — so every warded lot contains one complete self-contained maze, never a fragment of a neighboring one.

nodes.label: wards on land
nodes.comment: Ward lots gated to dry ground — where a lot runs into the sea, the water keeps its claim and the maze drowns.

nodes.label: the open wilds
nodes.comment: 1 minus the wards: the region every biome paints. Inside warded land the biomes leave the cells empty, which is exactly where the maze below shows through.

nodes.label: the wards
nodes.comment: The labyrinth itself, hedge walls over worn processional paths, one maze spanning each 6-chunk lot. It carves everywhere, but the biomes above bury it outside the warded lots. Two doors per edge and a little braid keep every ward walkable from the wilds.

nodes.label: script: scorch & breach
nodes.comment: What the fire did to the eastern wards: hedges become scorched stone, a third of every wall crumbles into ash-filled breaches, and the old paths vanish under ash. West of the emberline it paints nothing, leaving the hedges green.

nodes.label: the green march
nodes.comment: The unburnt world and the base coat: sea, sand shores, grass, bare rock on the steeps. It paints every cell outside warded land — including the whole ashfall, which the next biome overpaints.

nodes.label: ash & open
nodes.comment: The ashfall claims cells that are both east of the emberline and outside warded land.

nodes.label: the ashfall
nodes.comment: The same land after the fire: ash where grass would grow, gravel where beaches would lie, and the sea kept as water — the one thing on this side that did not burn. The region cut sits a little under the green march's so the ash wins the fractional slivers along drowned ward edges.

nodes.label: fen clumps
nodes.comment: Billowed continental-scale blobs deciding which stretches of the green coast drown into fen instead of keeping their beaches.

nodes.label: green fens
nodes.comment: Fen clumps gated to the green side — the ashfall coast is gravel, never marsh.

nodes.label: fen country
nodes.comment: And gated outside the wards, so no marsh creeps over a ward that runs down to the sea.

nodes.label: the drowning fens
nodes.comment: A biome used as a single-band painter: every tile empty except the shore, so all it paints is a wide marsh strip along the fen-country coastline, cut from coast distance so it keeps an even depth.

nodes.label: rivers of water
nodes.comment: The drainage dressed as water, painted over both countries — streams run freely through the hedge wards, and in the east the molten layer above will swallow all but the youngest trickles.

nodes.label: carved depth
nodes.comment: Uneroded minus eroded terrain: nonzero exactly where the rivers dug their valleys.

nodes.label: molten carve
nodes.comment: The carved band gated east of the emberline — the stretch of every valley that runs molten.

nodes.label: rivers of fire
nodes.comment: Lava wherever the eastern valleys are carved deep enough, overpainting the water below it. The same channel crosses the frontier and changes state — follow any river east and watch it catch.

nodes.label: char on land
nodes.comment: The emberline gradient gated to dry ground — its bands are the frontier habitats.

nodes.label: the burnt forest
nodes.comment: A strip of dead trees where the fire stopped — the woods that burned standing and never fell. Cross it and you know which country you are entering.

nodes.label: the warding stones
nodes.comment: Stone circles in a dotted line exactly along the char 0.5 contour: the line someone once held, and the fire respected — mostly. They are the oldest things in the marches.

nodes.label: green heights
nodes.comment: Eroded terrain gated to the green side: one field whose high band is the unburnt ridges and whose middle bands are the living lowlands. Every green settlement and creature below is a band of it.

nodes.label: watch outposts
nodes.comment: Rare towers on the green ridges, looking east. There are none in the ashfall — the eastern watch is what the scorched wards used to be.

nodes.label: outpost watch
nodes.comment: Sentries holding the same high band as their towers, walking back to their posts when you leave.

nodes.label: cottages
nodes.comment: Farmsteads across the mild green lowlands, and nowhere east of the stones — nobody rebuilds on ash.

nodes.label: the greenwood
nodes.comment: The living forest of the west, on the same band its burnt twin occupies at the frontier.

nodes.label: deer
nodes.comment: Meadow herds whose band overlaps the warded lots — deer graze inside the overgrown hedge mazes, which is the closest thing the wards still have to a keeper.

nodes.label: rabbits
nodes.comment: The low meadows near the coast, one band under the deer.

nodes.label: wolves
nodes.comment: Hunting the greenwood band and a little above it — between the deer and the outposts.

nodes.label: fen strip
nodes.comment: Coast distance gated to the green side: its just-above-0.5 band is the marshy waterline itself.

nodes.label: fen herons
nodes.comment: Stalking the first few tiles inland along the green coasts, quick to startle.

nodes.label: ash hounds
nodes.comment: The deep east belongs to the hounds: fast, far-sighted, and the reason to keep moving out there.

nodes.label: ember wisps
nodes.comment: Spawned from the molten carve field, so they drift along the rivers of fire — phasing through lava and ward walls alike, the only gentle things left in the east.

nodes.label: fallen wards
nodes.comment: Warded land east of the emberline — the scorched mazes.

nodes.label: ward sentries
nodes.comment: The garrison of the fallen wards, still walking the scorched corridors. They guard their spawn corridor and return to it — the last order they were given.
